name: PAKISTAN
lead: Pakistan sits where the Silk Road met the world's tallest peaks. Five of Earth's fourteen highest mountains stand here, yet the south has Arabian Sea beaches. More than 240 million people live here.
geo: The north has the Karakoram and Himalayan mountains. K2 is one of the hardest mountains to climb. Huge glaciers feed rivers that flow to the sea.
The south is very different. The Thar Desert bakes in the sun. The Indus Valley has fertile plains of wheat, cotton and sugarcane.
animals: The snow leopard is so shy that people call it the 'ghost of the mountains'. Pakistan has one of the world's largest wild populations, living above 3,000 m.
The Indus blind dolphin uses sonar because the river is too muddy to see. The markhor, a wild goat with corkscrew horns, is the national animal.
culture: Drivers paint trucks with blazing colours, flowers, portraits and poems, so the roads become rolling art galleries. Fresh naan drifts out of clay tandoor ovens in every bazaar.
Cricket matches stop traffic, and the whole country watches together. At Eid, families share biryani and sweet sheer khurma, wear new clothes and visit neighbours.
history: The Indus Valley Civilisation flourished at Mohenjo-daro over 4,500 years ago. Its people had running water and brick houses. Alexander the Great later marched through these passes.
The Mughal Empire built grand mosques and the glittering Lahore Fort. In 1947, Pakistan became independent when British India was divided.
wows: Pakistan grows over 1.8 million tonnes of mangoes a year.
K2 is nicknamed the Savage Mountain because it is so dangerous.
Mohenjo-daro had covered drains nearly 2,000 years before Rome's sewers.
The Karakoram Highway climbs to 4,714 m, one of the highest paved roads.
The Mirror Palace in Lahore Fort glitters with thousands of mirror chips.
Pakistan has over 7,000 glaciers, among the most outside the poles.
Ten Nepali climbers made the first winter climb of K2 in 2021.

myths.fact: Polo began in Asia. Teams still play every summer at Shandur Pass, 3,700 m up.

myths.myth: Urdu and Hindi are totally different languages
myths.fact: Spoken every day, they sound almost the same. Only the writing and some formal words differ.
